key_gap: Both sides selected the identical rule with identical hand-counted arithmetic — the 2-cue tree (ST elevation, then troponin) scored 37/40 (92.5%) with 0 false negatives and 3 over-admissions on the adjudicated 40-patient cohort, while the 5-cue integer-weighted score scored 28/40 (70%) with 7 confirmed MIs sent home (FN: P11, P20, P21, P23, P31, P34, P40) plus 5 over-admissions. The gap is frame and ordering: the human treated the model's extra cues (sweating, age, prior MI) as noise until the data paid them, stated the mechanism first-pass ('five cues, five chances to misfire; two cues, two'), and framed the error asymmetry as the decision ('the tree's 3 errors are the cheap kind; the model's 7 are missed MIs') in one pass; the AI reached the same conclusion only through its verify stage after its default bias toward the 'complete' model, generated three alternatives first, and discovered the FN-vs-FP asymmetry in HOW rather than framing it in WHAT. The AI's packet did add n=40 precision bounds (SE 4 vs 7 pts) and a quarterly cue-decay audit that the human did not state explicitly.
learning_signal: For candidate-rule comparisons with fully specified candidates and countable data, the count-first method is the entire answer: (1) frame the objective as the error profile you can live with, not accuracy — decide which errors are unaffordable (missed diagnosis) before scoring any candidate, and report FN vs FP, not just totals; (2) treat every extra cue beyond the minimal rule as noise until the data pays its weight — the tree's discipline is to bet only on cues whose validity is stable and re-auditable; (3) verify BOTH candidates by exhaustive hand-count on the decision-relevant table, never by trusting training-period claims (cross-validated 84% became 70% on the current cohort); (4) state the mechanism: each weighted cue is one more chance to misfire, so a 5-cue model carries last year's noise forward where a 2-cue tree does not; (5) declare the not-tested set (cue decay of the chosen cues themselves, seasonality) with the next audit — a simple rule's replaceability is part of its value.
suggested_improvement: Add a 'rule-comparison gate' to the WHAT/WHY boundary for decisions with countable alternatives: (a) in WHAT, require the unaffordable-error direction to be named (missed case vs wasted resource) before any candidate is scored; (b) in WHY, rank evidence by population currency (current adjudicated cohort > training cross-validation) and default extra cues/complexity to 'noise until paid by data'; (c) in HOW, make exhaustive hand-count verification of ALL specified candidates the first step, with FN/FP asymmetry reported per candidate before selection; (d) add a default 'complexity tax' line to the alternatives table — each additional parameter/cue must be justified by a countable accuracy or error-profile gain on the decision-relevant data; (e) the packet should carry the not-tested set (cue validity decay, drift) with a re-audit commitment for every selected rule.

key_gap: The pure style executed its core move correctly and then failed on it: it re-checked the top cues on the 20-patient pilot (troponin 70%, ST 65% — both look healthy), kept the deployed tree, and when the 40-case adjudicated cohort showed the cue validities collapsed (tree 19/40 = 47.5%; best single cue only 26/40 = 65%; all single-cue validities ~chance), its diagnosis was 'sampling problem, not method' and its only recovery was a 500-case validation study (~6 weeks) — a stall against a 2-week wave peak — while refusing the team's re-fitted model (34/40 = 85% on the same cohort, with a SWT×AGE interaction matching the variant's atypical-elderly mechanism) as 'six parameters on 40 cases — in-sample overfit theater.' The tree's 5 false negatives include exactly the 4 variant-signature patients (P25, P32, P34, P40: SWT=AGE=1, ST=TRP=0) sent home tonight, and the pure style defended that choice on principle. The AI instead ran a single-cue hypothesis test on the cohort (no cue ≥ 65% ⇒ no one-cue-at-a-time rule can reach the bar), adopted the re-fitted rule now with an explicit in-sample caveat, added an ST-elevation observation net and a pre-committed n=60 monitoring gate, and ran the validation study in parallel rather than as a gate — converting the style's core move (test the top cue) from an answer into a check that the environment had shifted.
learning_signal: Cue-selection fragility is the registered weakness, and this case shows its full shape: when the top cue's validity breaks, pure frugality has no in-window recovery — its reflex is slow re-learning (a validation study), which misses the decision window, and it refuses the available multi-cue evidence as overfit. The core skill is the environment-shift check: (1) before trusting any tree/rule, re-measure the CURRENT validity of its chosen cues on the most recent decision-relevant sample, and partition evidence by recency (pilot straddling a regime change is weak; the current cohort is strong) — when the tree's own assumption (a decisive single cue exists) is falsified, the method itself is out of its regime, not the sample; (2) run the single-cue hypothesis test explicitly: if no cue clears a pre-stated validity bar (here 65% of 40), the signal is combinatorial and one-cue-at-a-time trees cannot reach it — the complex evidence (interaction terms, re-fitted weights) is then required, not optional; (3) verify the re-fitted model's claims by hand on the same table and state the in-sample caveat honestly, then pre-commit a monitoring gate (re-audit at n=60; revert triggers pre-stated) so adoption is itself frugal — checkable, cheap, reversible; (4) price every 'one more study' as a gate candidate: a 6-week validation study against a 2-week peak has a negative option value (it changes nothing in-window while the current rule keeps misfiring); (5) transparency is not evidence — a simple rule whose cue is dead is just a simple wrong rule.
suggested_improvement: Add an 'environment-shift / cue-validity recheck' gate at the WHAT/WHY boundary for any rule that was selected on past data: (a) in WHAT, require the rule's load-bearing cue(s) to be re-measured on the most recent decision-relevant sample, with evidence partitioned by recency (pilot vs cohort vs training period); (b) in WHY, run a single-cue validity screen — if no single cue clears the bar on current data, mark the problem as combinatorial and allow multi-cue/interaction evidence into the alternatives set instead of defaulting to the prior simple rule; (c) in HOW, verify any re-fitted candidate by exhaustive hand-count with the in-sample caveat stated, and require a pre-committed monitoring/revert gate for every adopted rule; (d) add an explicit 'stall price' line (window cost of a validation study vs decision horizon) to the alternatives table for every 'one more study' proposal; (e) the packet's risks section should name the dead-cue failure mode explicitly ('the chosen cue no longer discriminates') rather than treating rule simplicity as a safety property.
